craft_notes: Sthāyin: resolve (the steadied mind). Sanskrit first: condition (placed, steadied), clearance (obstruction left), result (mark pointed) → L4 sets condition line 1, clearance+result line 2. Rows: row 3 (until/then correlative kept as till/then). Rupture: dash after 'clear' — steadiness held, release follows. Close: colon landing on nearness ('shines near' — the mark approaches). Minimal pass: 'unknotted' for tyakta (obstruction untied, singable); zero doctrine change. Read aloud: line 1 stills (till/unmoved/clear long vowels), dash, line 2 quickens to the mark. Rejected: 'the mark is shown' — killed: vinirdiśet points out, active prescription kept; 'when winds are tamed' — killed: taming imports mastery, Sanskrit says left-behind.

lines: Set the mind there till it stands unmoved and clear —
the winds unknotted: then the mark shines near.
l4.sanskrit_cite: tanmadhye nikṣipec cittaṃ yāvat tatra sthirīkṛtam / tyaktaruddho yadā vāyustadā lakṣaṃ vinirdiśet

reads_against.argmap: The mark is assigned when mind is steadied there and the wind handled.
c1_essence: Mind steadied in the middle, obstruction gone — then the mark is given.
reads_against.c1_rasa: adbhuta with vīra-utsāha (wonder braced by resolve)
